ROC curve and AUC for edge recovery

Source: R/eval.R
roc_auc.Rd

Computes the ROC curve of a score matrix against a true adjacency matrix, using the upper triangle. The curve steps only at distinct score values, so tied scores are handled correctly: a block of tied edges gives one diagonal segment, i.e. each tied positive/negative pair counts 1/2. The AUC therefore equals the Mann-Whitney statistic and does not depend on the order of the edges.

Usage

roc_auc(score_mat, truth_mat)

Arguments

score_mat

Numeric p x p matrix of edge scores (higher = more likely an edge), or a vector of edge scores.

truth_mat

p x p matrix of true edges (non-zero = edge), or a vector matching score_mat.

Value

A list with FPR and TPR (the curve, from (0, 0) to (1, 1)), thresholds (the score at each point; Inf for the origin) and auc. If the truth has no edges or no non-edges, the curve is the diagonal and auc is NA.

Details

Ties matter for sparse estimators, which give many edges a score of exactly 0 (and PIPs that underflow to exactly 0 or 1). An implementation that accumulates one edge at a time in sorted order breaks ties by matrix position and can be off by several hundredths of AUC.

Edges with a missing score or truth are dropped.

Examples

truth <- matrix(0, 5, 5); truth[1, 2] <- truth[2, 3] <- 1
truth <- truth + t(truth)
score <- matrix(0, 5, 5); score[1, 2] <- 0.9; score[3, 4] <- 0.9
score <- score + t(score)
roc_auc(score, truth)$auc   # ties at 0.9 and at 0 count 1/2
#> [1] 0.6875
